title: Terraform firewall, DNS and IPS resources: EUN fields, DNS categories, custom signatures

checks.do: Whether a rule's EUN template was set in the console before blaming the provider for a plan difference.
Whether custom IPS signature text starts at `alert` with literal networks and a `sid` of at least 1000000.
Whether a PREDEFINED network service was imported before it was referenced.

eun-fields-optional-not-computed.statement: In v4.8.8 the firewall filtering rule schema declares `eun_template_id` as Optional, with no Computed flag.

quotes: Description: "The EUN template ID associated with the rule",

eun-docs-asymmetry.statement: The data-source page lists both EUN attributes while the resource page's argument reference does not mention them.

quotes: * `eun_template_id` - (Integer) The ID of the Enhanced User Notification (EUN) template associated with the rule.

eun-read-and-expand.statement: Read copies the API's `eunTemplateId` into state, and the SDK model tags that field `omitempty`.

quotes: _ = d.Set("eun_template_id", resp.EUNTemplateID)
EUNTemplateID int `json:"eunTemplateId,omitempty"`

dns-category-match-check-removed.statement: Provider v4.8.2 removed the local validation on `zia_firewall_dns_rule` that forced `dest_ip_categories` and `res_categories` to match because of an old API requirement.

quotes: Removed local validation on resource `zia_firewall_dns_rule` that forced both attribute values `dest_ip_categories` and `res_categories` to match due to old API requirement.

dns-category-historical-comment.statement: The DNS rule source still carries commented-out text saying the API returns `INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT` with "Requested IP-Categories and Resolved Domain Categories aren't matching" when the two sets differ.

quotes: // it returns INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT: "Requested IP-Categories and Resolved Domain Categories aren't matching".

ips-signature-validated-first.statement: `zia_ips_signature_rules` validates `rule_text` against the Zscaler validation endpoint on every create and update; a rejected rule aborts before any state is written and the API diagnostic is surfaced.

quotes: If the rule text is rejected, the create/update aborts before any state is written
ipsSignaturesValidateEndpoint = "/zia/api/v1/ipsSignatureRules/validateRuleText"

ips-signature-syntax-limits.statement: The validation endpoint requires literal `any` or a CIDR rather than Suricata variables like `$HOME_NET`, a `sid` of at least 1000000, both `msg` and `sid`, the `->` direction only, and no leading whitespace before `alert`.

quotes: Suricata variables such as `$EXTERNAL_NET` and `$HOME_NET` are not defined
The custom-signature `sid` range starts at `1000000`.
`msg:"..."` and `sid:N` are required inside the parentheses.
The bidirectional `<>` operator is not supported.
No leading whitespace before `alert`.

ips-signature-whitespace-normalized.statement: The provider normalizes leading and trailing whitespace and trailing newlines in `rule_text` on both sides of the diff, but an indent-stripping heredoc whose rule line is indented more than the closing marker leaves spaces that the endpoint rejects with `Unexpected character(s) at rule header`.

quotes: `rule_text` is whitespace-insensitive across plans.
the leftover spaces become part of the string and Zscaler's validation endpoint rejects the rule

destination-group-custom-categories-only.statement: The `ip_categories` attribute of `zia_firewall_filtering_destination_groups` accepts only custom URL categories.

quotes: The `ip_categories` attribute only accepts custom URL categories.

predefined-service-import-first.statement: A `PREDEFINED` network service is built into ZIA and must be imported before Terraform runs; trying to update it directly returns `DUPLICATE_ITEM`.

quotes: are built-in resources within the ZIA cloud and must be imported before the Terraform execution.
Attempting to update the resource directly will return `DUPLICATE_ITEM` error message.

eun-contract-vs-go-and-terraform.summary: Whether the firewall filtering rule contract carries the EUN fields.

positions.says: The Automate contract lists `eunTemplateId` and `isEunEnabled` as absent from the rule family's contract fields.

quotes: **Go SDK fields absent from the contract:** `accessControl`, `enableFullLogging`, `endPointApplicationGroups`, `endPointApplications`, `eunTemplateId`
IsEUNEnabled bool `json:"isEunEnabled,omitempty"`

eun-contract-vs-go-and-terraform.impact: Do not use the published contract to say whether a firewall rule accepts an EUN template; the SDK and provider send it.

issue-605-plan-diff.title: Whether a rule whose HCL omits `eun_template_id` plans a change to null while the apply leaves the tenant value unchanged
issue-605-plan-diff.blocks: saying that an omitted EUN template produces a permanent plan difference on a firewall rule
issue-605-plan-diff.detail: Unverified legacy statement: upstream issue 605 reports a plan showing `eun_template_id = <id> -> null` on a rule whose HCL omits it, with apply leaving the value unchanged; this is operator-reported and not reproduced. Apply a rule with a template set in the console, omit it in HCL and plan.

dns-categories-backend-acceptance.title: Whether the backend accepts different `dest_ip_categories` and `res_categories` sets on a DNS rule
dns-categories-backend-acceptance.blocks: saying that DNS rule category sets no longer have to match
dns-categories-backend-acceptance.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the provider no longer checks locally, but the source still carries text saying a mismatch returns INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT; universal backend acceptance is not established. Create a DNS rule with different sets in a scratch tenant.
